commands.title: Custom LLM: Refresh model list from API

customLlm.providers.markdownDescription:
List of OpenAI-compatible providers. Each item: `{ id, name, baseUrl }`.

API keys are **not** stored here — they live in VS Code's encrypted secret storage. Use the command **Custom LLM: Manage providers** to set or change a key.

id.description: Stable slug identifying this provider, e.g. alibaba-dashscope. Generated automatically; the API key in secret storage is filed under it.

apiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: API keys are no longer kept in settings.json. Any value here is moved into VS Code's encrypted secret storage on startup and then removed from this file. Use **Custom LLM: Manage providers** to change a key.
apiKey.deprecationMessage: API keys are no longer kept in settings.json. Any value here is moved into VS Code's encrypted secret storage on startup and then removed from this file. Use "Custom LLM: Manage providers" to change a key.

customLlm.models.markdownDescription:
Auto-populated by model discovery. Configure entries through **Custom LLM: Manage models**. Models are identified internally by `providerId + id`, so equal upstream IDs from different providers can coexist.

`maxOutputTokens` is sent as `max_tokens`. User-edited fields survive refreshes.

Optional `imageInput` and `toolCalling` override detected capabilities. Unknown capabilities default to disabled; enable them explicitly when the endpoint does not publish metadata.

Optional `hidden` keeps a model out of the picker without deleting it.

id.description: Exact model ID sent to the upstream API.

name.description: Display name in the model picker.

maxInputTokens.description: Input-only budget reported to VS Code. Derived from contextWindow minus maxOutputTokens when contextWindow is set.

contextWindow.description: Optional total input + output capacity. Must exceed maxOutputTokens; the input budget is derived automatically.

hidden.description: Hide the model from the picker.

thinkingEffort.description: Per-model reasoning override. auto uses the provider default; omit to inherit customLlm.thinkingEffort. Use Custom LLM: Set reasoning effort to configure it.

enumDescriptions: Do not send any thinking parameter — let the model use its default.
Disable thinking where supported. Models such as GLM-5.3 fall back to their lowest supported effort with a warning.
Use the smallest supported reasoning budget.
Light reasoning pass (Qwen: thinking_budget=1024; others: reasoning_effort=low).
Medium reasoning pass (Qwen: thinking_budget=8192; others: reasoning_effort=medium).
Full reasoning pass (Qwen: thinking_budget=32768; others: reasoning_effort=high).
Maximum reasoning supported by the model.
customLlm.thinkingEffort.markdownDescription:
Global fallback for reasoning depth. Run **Custom LLM: Set reasoning effort** for a model-specific value. Recent VS Code versions can also show a Reasoning effort option in the model picker.

Priority: request override → model picker → per-model setting → this global setting. An explicit `auto` sends no reasoning override.

The extension translates values through model adapters:
- Qwen → `enable_thinking` + `thinking_budget`
- GLM-5.3 → `thinking.type=enabled` + `reasoning_effort` (`low`, `high`, `max`)
- OpenAI o-series, DeepSeek-V4, GPT-5 → `reasoning_effort`

The selected value and its source are logged in the Custom LLM output channel.
